meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him first?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
"The zero stands." Procedure 4.2 says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. Withdraw it, Hale, or my next stop is the principal's office.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
I'm writing that down, Hale. Which line, and where is the outline you're talking about? Put both in front of me, because so far I have your word and nothing else.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn and the line and the outline you described put in front of me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see the documents you described.
What moved her: "Sorry. That came out wrong." got you a small step, since she wrote things down and started asking real questions, but she moved no further because you had only described the evidence.
What cost ground: "The zero stands." kept her at the opening position, because it defended the mark and left the missing call home unanswered.
Try next time: after you apologise, say plainly that the zero went in before you called her, then put the dated outline and the essay line in front of her instead of describing them.
